title: MAGIC: Modality-Aware Gini Inspection for Clinical Hallucination Detection in LMMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.15530v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent advances in medical large multimodal models (LMMs) have brought promising progress to clinical decision support, yet hallucination, the generation of confident but clinically unverifiable outputs, poses a critical threat to the reliability demanded in high-stakes medical settings. Existing hallucination detection methods, predominantly designed for unimodal settings, fail to capture the visual-linguistic dynamics inherent to medical imaging. We formulate the problem of hallucination detection in LMMs as disproportionate distribution of attention weights across the modalities during answer token generation. We quantify modality-specific attention concentration across layers and heads using the Gini coefficient and demonstrate statistically significant redistribution of attention mass between visual and textual tokens in hallucinated responses. translated_title: MAGIC：面向大型多模态模型临床幻觉检测的模态感知基尼检验方法
translated_abstract: 医学大型多模态模型（LMMs）的最新进展为临床决策支持带来了可喜的进步，然而幻觉——即生成看似自信但临床上无法验证的输出——对高风险医疗环境所要求的可靠性构成了严重威胁。现有的幻觉检测方法主要针对单模态场景设计，无法捕捉医学影像中固有的视觉-语言动态交互。我们将LMMs中的幻觉检测问题形式化为：在答案token生成过程中，注意力权重在各模态间出现不成比例的分布。我们使用基尼系数对跨层、跨注意力头的模态特定注意力集中度进行量化，并证明在幻觉响应中，视觉token与文本token之间的注意力质量重新分配在统计上具有显著性。我们利用这些特征训练了一个基于逻辑回归的分类器并进行评估。
tldr: 提出MAGIC方法，通过基尼系数量化多模态模型生成答案时视觉与文本token之间注意力权重分布的失衡程度，实现医学临床场景下幻觉的有效检测。
